newsitem.title: UK: Barclays says buyback keeps equity tight.
newsitem.headline: Barclays says buyback keeps equity tight.

text.p: Barclays Plc's 26 million share buyback is designed to keep its equity base tight and should be seen as an investment for shareholders who do not sell, chief executive Martin Taylor said on Wednesday.

"We want to keep our equity base tight," Taylor said in an interview. "This is an investment on behalf of the shareholders who don't sell. I'm much more interested in them, their holding in the company is concentrated."
Taylor noted that Barclays had changed to a system of buying through principal rather than agency brokers, making the sales subject to the usual capital gains tax rules.
Last week, Barclays said it would return around 500 million stg of capital to shareholders in the next twelve months.
The current operation, which will cost around 290 million stg, will take Barclays' share repurchases to around 1.25 billion stg since the programme began in August 1995.
"We've been buying shares in a very high quality financial institution without paying a premium," Taylor said.
Barclays shares leapt on the announcement, reaching a high of 1158p but by 0955 GMT they had settled back to be quoted unchanged at 1122 in small volume.
